html:
A Mende doctor, the first from the protectorate to qualify, who led the Sierra Leone People's Party and became the first prime minister when Sierra Leone became independent on 27 April 1961.

His party united chiefs and educated men of the interior, and he balanced their interests with those of the Krio of Freetown, who had long led politics. His rule was mild and he kept the parliamentary system Britain left. He died in office in 1964, and his brother Albert Margai succeeded him. The SLPP's defeat in the 1967 election brought Siaka Stevens to power. See also decolonisation and the British Empire.
sum: A Mende doctor, the first from the protectorate to qualify, who led the Sierra Leone People's Party and became the first prime minister when Sierra Leone became independent on 27 April 1961.
